1	---
2	title: generateStaticParams
3	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4	---
5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18	
19	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20	    slug: post.slug,
21	  }))
22	}
23	
24	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26	export default async function Page({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { slug } = await params
32	  // ...
33	}
34	```
35	
36	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40	
41	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42	    slug: post.slug,
43	  }))
44	}
45	
46	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49	  const { slug } = await params
50	  // ...
51	}
52	```
53	
54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62	
63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70	
71	## Returns
72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74	
75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77	
78	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83	
84	## Single Dynamic Segment
85	
86	```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
87	export function generateStaticParams() {
88	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
89	}
90	
91	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
92	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
93	// - /product/1
94	// - /product/2
95	// - /product/3
96	export default async function Page({
97	  params,
98	}: {
99	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
100	}) {
101	  const { id } = await params
102	  // ...
103	}
104	```
105	
106	```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
107	export function generateStaticParams() {
108	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
109	}
110	
111	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
112	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
113	// - /product/1
114	// - /product/2
115	// - /product/3
116	export default async function Page({ params }) {
117	  const { id } = await params
118	  // ...
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Multiple Dynamic Segments
123	
124	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
125	export function generateStaticParams() {
126	  return [
127	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
128	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
129	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
130	  ]
131	}
132	
133	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
134	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
135	// - /products/a/1
136	// - /products/b/2
137	// - /products/c/3
138	export default async function Page({
139	  params,
140	}: {
141	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
142	}) {
143	  const { category, product } = await params
144	  // ...
145	}
146	```
147	
148	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
149	export function generateStaticParams() {
150	  return [
151	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
152	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
153	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
154	  ]
155	}
156	
157	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
158	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
159	// - /products/a/1
160	// - /products/b/2
161	// - /products/c/3
162	export default async function Page({ params }) {
163	  const { category, product } = await params
164	  // ...
165	}
166	```
167	
168	## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
169	
170	```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
171	export function generateStaticParams() {
172	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
173	}
174	
175	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
176	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
177	// - /product/a/1
178	// - /product/b/2
179	// - /product/c/3
180	export default async function Page({
181	  params,
182	}: {
183	  params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
184	}) {
185	  const { slug } = await params
186	  // ...
187	}
188	```
189	
190	```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher
191	export function generateStaticParams() {
192	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
193	}
194	
195	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
196	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
197	// - /product/a/1
198	// - /product/b/2
199	// - /product/c/3
200	export default async function Page({ params }) {
201	  const { slug } = await params
202	  // ...
203	}
204	```
205	
206	## Examples
207	
208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
213	
214	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
215	export async function generateStaticParams() {
216	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
217	
218	  return posts.map((post) => ({
219	    slug: post.slug,
220	  }))
221	}
222	```
223	
224	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
225	export async function generateStaticParams() {
226	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
227	
228	  return posts.map((post) => ({
229	    slug: post.slug,
230	  }))
231	}
232	```
233	
234	#### Subset of paths at build time
235	
236	To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
237	
238	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
239	export async function generateStaticParams() {
240	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
241	
242	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
243	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
244	    slug: post.slug,
245	  }))
246	}
247	```
248	
249	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
250	export async function generateStaticParams() {
251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252	
253	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```
259	
260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```
275	
276	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
277	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
278	export const dynamicParams = false
279	
280	export async function generateStaticParams() {
281	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
282	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
283	
284	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
285	    slug: post.slug,
286	  }))
287	}
288	```
289	
290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```
334	
335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
336	export async function generateStaticParams() {
337	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
338	}
339	
340	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
341	  const { id } = await params
342	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
343	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
344	}
345	```
346	
347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
352	export async function generateStaticParams() {
353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}
355	
356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```
371	
372	See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
373	
374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
390	
391	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
392	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
393	export async function generateStaticParams() {
394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```
410	
411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
412	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
432	// Generate segments for [category]
433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))
458	}
459	
460	export default function Layout({ params }) {
461	  // ...
462	}
463	```
464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
470	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	> **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
516	
517	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
518	
519	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
520	export async function generateStaticParams({
521	  params: { category },
522	}: {
523	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
524	}) {
525	  const products = await fetch(
526	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
527	  ).then((res) => res.json())
528	
529	  return products.map((product) => ({
530	    product: product.id,
531	  }))
532	}
533	```
534	
535	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
536	
537	## Version History
538	
539	| Version   | Changes                            |
540	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
541	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

1	---
2	title: useRouter
3	description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
4	---
5	
6	The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).
7	
8	> **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.
9	
10	```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
11	'use client'
12	
13	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
14	
15	export default function Page() {
16	  const router = useRouter()
17	
18	  return (
19	    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
20	      Dashboard
21	    </button>
22	  )
23	}
24	```
25	
26	```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
27	'use client'
28	
29	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
30	
31	export default function Page() {
32	  const router = useRouter()
33	
34	  return (
35	    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
36	      Dashboard
37	    </button>
38	  )
39	}
40	```
41	
42	## `useRouter()`
43	
44	- `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
45	- `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.

---
title: useRouter
description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
---

The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).

> **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.

```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

## `useRouter()`

- `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
- `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
- `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
- `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).
- `router.back()`: Navigate back to the previous route in the browser’s history stack.
- `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.
- `router.bfcacheId`: An opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations. See [`bfcacheId`](#bfcacheid) below for details.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - You must not send untrusted or unsanitized URLs to `router.push` or `router.replace`, as this can open your site to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. For example, `javascript:` URLs sent to `router.push` or `router.replace` will be executed in the context of your page.
> - The `<Link>` component automatically prefetch routes as they become visible in the viewport.
> - `refresh()` could re-produce the same result if fetch requests are cached. Other Request-time APIs like `cookies` and `headers` could also change the response.
> - The `onInvalidate` callback is called at most once per prefetch request. It signals when you may want to trigger a new prefetch for updated route data.

### Migrating from `next/router`

- The `useRouter` hook should be imported from `next/navigation` and not `next/router` when using the App Router
- The `pathname` string has been removed and is replaced by [`usePathname()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname)
- The `query` object has been removed and is replaced by [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params)
- `router.events` has been replaced. [See below.](#router-events)

[View the full migration guide](/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration).

## Examples

### Router events

You can listen for page changes by composing other Client Component hooks like `usePathname` and `useSearchParams`.

```jsx filename="app/components/navigation-events.js"
'use client'

import { useEffect } from 'react'
import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'

export function NavigationEvents() {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const searchParams = useSearchParams()

  useEffect(() => {
    const url = `${pathname}?${searchParams}`
    console.log(url)
    // You can now use the current URL
    // ...
  }, [pathname, searchParams])

  return '...'
}
```

Which can be imported into a layout.

```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={2,10-12}
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { NavigationEvents } from './components/navigation-events'

export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}

        <Suspense fallback={null}>
          <NavigationEvents />
        </Suspense>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

> **Good to know**: `<NavigationEvents>` is wrapped in a [`Suspense` boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#examples) because[`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) causes client-side rendering up to the closest `Suspense` boundary during [prerendering](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering). [Learn more](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params#behavior).

### Disabling scroll to top

By default, Next.js will scroll to the top of the page when navigating to a new route. You can disable this behavior by passing `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.

```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
    >
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.jsx" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
    >
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

### `bfcacheId`

`router.bfcacheId` is an opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations.

The recommended use is to pass it as a React `key` to opt out of state preservation on fresh navigations, while still restoring it during a back/forward navigation:

```tsx filename="app/example/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const { bfcacheId } = useRouter()
  return <form key={bfcacheId}>{/* ... */}</form>
}
```

When `cacheComponents` is enabled, the App Router preserves Client Component state across navigations using React `<Activity>`. Keying a component on `bfcacheId` resets it on each fresh navigation while still preserving its state across browser back/forward navigations. See [Preserving UI state](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for the recommended per-pattern resets.

> **Good to know**:
> Instead of `bfcacheId`, prefer resetting state explicitly in an event handler (for example, `onSubmit`) or deriving a key from your data (for example, a draft id from the server). Use `bfcacheId` only as a last resort, like when migrating an existing codebase.

## Version History

| Version   | Changes                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v15.4.0` | Optional `onInvalidate` callback for `router.prefetch` introduced |
| `v13.0.0` | `useRouter` from `next/navigation` introduced.                    |

--- title: userAgent description: The userAgent helper extends the Web Request API with additional properties and methods to interact with the user agent object from the request. --- {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `Content` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */} The `userAgent` helper extends the [Web Request API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) with additional properties and methods to interact with the user agent object from the request. ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher import { NextRequest, NextResponse, userAgent } from 'next/server' export function proxy(request: NextRequest) { const url = request.nextUrl const { device } = userAgent(request) // device.type can be: 'mobile', 'tablet', 'console', 'smarttv', // 'wearable', 'embedded', or undefined (for desktop browsers) const viewport = device.type || 'desktop' url.searchParams.set('viewport', viewport) return NextResponse.rewrite(url) } ``` ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher import { NextResponse, userAgent } from 'next/server' export function proxy(request) { const url = request.nextUrl const { device } = userAgent(request) // device.type can be: 'mobile', 'tablet', 'console', 'smarttv', // 'wearable', 'embedded', or undefined (for desktop browsers) const viewport = device.type || 'desktop' url.searchParams.set('viewport', viewport) return NextResponse.rewrite(url) } ``` ## `isBot` A boolean indicating whether the request comes from a known bot. ## `browser` An object containing information about the browser used in the request. - `name`: A string representing the browser's name, or `undefined` if not identifiable. - `version`: A string representing the browser's version, or `undefined`. ## `device` An object containing information about the device used in the request. - `model`: A string representing the model of the device, or `undefined`. - `type`: A string representing the type of the device, such as `console`, `mobile`, `tablet`, `smarttv`, `wearable`, `embedded`, or `undefined`. - `vendor`: A string representing the vendor of the device, or `undefined`. === HEADERS === --- title: headers description: API reference for the headers function. --- `headers` is an **async** function that allows you to **read** the HTTP incoming request headers from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const headersList = await headers() const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const headersList = await headers() const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') } ``` ## Reference ### Parameters `headers` does not take any parameters. ### Returns `headers` returns a **read-only** [Web Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers) object. - [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. ## Good to know - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)**. - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `headers()` outside of a [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options. ## Examples ### Using the Authorization header ```jsx filename="app/page.js" import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const authorization = (await headers()).get('authorization') const res = await fetch('...', { headers: { authorization }, // Forward the authorization header }) const user = await res.json() return

{user.name}

} ``` ## Version History | Version | Changes | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `v15.0.0-RC` | `headers` is now an async function. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | | `v13.0.0` | `headers` introduced. |

title: Route Segment Config
description: Learn about how to configure options for Next.js route segments.
---

The Route Segment Config options allow you to configure the behavior of a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) by directly exporting the following variables:

| Option                                                                                             | Type                                                              | Default                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams)     | `boolean`                                                         | `true`                     |
| [`runtime`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime)                 | `'nodejs' \| 'edge' (deprecated)`                                 | `'nodejs'`                 |
| [`preferredRegion`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/preferredRegion) | `'auto' \| 'global' \| 'home' \| string \| string[] (deprecated)` | `'auto'`                   |
| [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration)         | `number`                                                          | Set by deployment platform |

## Version History

| Version      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v16.0.0`    | `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` removed when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. See [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config). |
| `v16.0.0`    | `export const experimental_ppr = true` removed. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-experimental_ppr-route-segment-config-from-app-router-pages-and-layouts) is available.                                                                                                  |
| `v15.0.0-RC` | `export const runtime = "experimental-edge"` deprecated. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#transform-app-router-route-segment-config-runtime-value-from-experimental-edge-to-edge) is available.                                                                                 |

---
title: CSS
description: Learn about the different ways to add CSS to your application, including Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, Global CSS, and more.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about the alternatives ways you can use CSS in your application.
  links:
    - app/guides/tailwind-v3-css
    - app/guides/sass
    - app/guides/css-in-js
---

Next.js provides several ways to style your application using CSS, including:

- [Tailwind CSS](#tailwind-css)
- [CSS Modules](#css-modules)
- [Global CSS](#global-css)
- [External Stylesheets](#external-stylesheets)
- [Sass](/docs/app/guides/sass)
- [CSS-in-JS](/docs/app/guides/css-in-js)

## Tailwind CSS

[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) is a utility-first CSS framework that provides low-level utility classes to build custom designs.

<AppOnly>

Install Tailwind CSS:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm add -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss
```

```bash package="npm"
npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn add -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss
```

```bash package="bun"
bun add -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss
```

Add the PostCSS plugin to your `postcss.config.mjs` file:

```js filename="postcss.config.mjs"
export default {
  plugins: {
    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {},
  },
}
```

Import Tailwind in your global CSS file:

```css filename="app/globals.css"
@import 'tailwindcss';
```

content.text:
Migration is complete and verified. `pages/` is gone.

## New structure

```
app/layout.tsx            ← _app.js + _document.js
app/page.tsx              ← pages/index.js
app/blog/page.tsx         ← pages/blog/index.js
app/blog/[id]/page.tsx    ← pages/blog/[id].js
app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx ← router.isFallback branch
app/not-found.tsx         ← pages/404.js
app/error.tsx             ← pages/_error.js
app/api/posts/route.ts        ← pages/api/posts/index.js
app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts   ← pages/api/posts/[id].js
app/api/posts/types.ts        (ApiPost)
lib/posts.ts                  (typed data access: Post, PostComment)
components/AppProvider.tsx    ← components/AppProvider.js
components/NavButton.tsx, BackButton.tsx  (extracted client interactivity)
```

## Pages Router APIs replaced

Per AGENTS.md I read the bundled docs for this build (16.4.0-canary.20) before writing code, which changed several choices:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `getServerSideProps` (used `req.headers`) | async Server Component + `await headers()` |
| `getStaticProps` + `revalidate` | segment config `export const revalidate = 60 / 300` |
| `getStaticPaths` | `generateStaticParams` |
| `fallback: 'blocking'` | `export const dynamicParams = true` |
| `next/head` | Metadata API (`metadata`, `generateMetadata`) |
| `next/router` | `useRouter` from `next/navigation` |
| `router.isFallback` | `loading.tsx` |
| `_error.js` `statusCode` | `error.tsx` with the **`retry`** prop (stable in 16.3; not `reset`) |
| API Routes (`req`/`res`, manual 405) | Route Handlers; `params` is a `Promise`; unhandled methods auto-405, auto-`OPTIONS` sets `Allow` |
| Google Fonts `<link>` in `_document` | `next/font/google` self-hosted, wired through `--font-inter` in `globals.css` |

Types are explicit throughout (`params: Promise<{ id: string }>`, `Metadata`, `ReactNode`, typed API/data interfaces) rather than relying on the generated `PageProps`/`RouteContext` globals, so typechecking doesn't depend on `next typegen` having run.

Two notes on judgment calls: the bundled migration guide still says app-dir `fetch` defaults to `force-cache`, but `fetch.md` for this version says caching is opt-in — so static behavior comes from the `revalidate` segment exports, confirmed by the build output. And `PUT /api/posts/[id]` treats an empty/unparseable body as "no changes" to match the original's all-fields-optional semantics, while `POST /api/posts` still 400s on invalid JSON.

## Verification

- `next build` ✓ — 15/15 pages; `/blog` at 1m, `/blog/[id]` SSG ×10 at 5m, `/` and both API routes dynamic
- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Live `next start` checks: all pages render (SSR timestamp + user-agent on `/`, metadata titles, self-hosted woff2, `notFound()` UI for `/blog/9999`, on-demand `/blog/42`, 404 for unknown routes); all API methods correct incl. 201/400/405 and `OPTIONS` → `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST`

I stopped the verification server and added `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `*.tsbuildinfo` to `.gitignore` since the TS/App Router setup now generates them. Nothing is committed — the working tree holds the staged `pages/` deletions and the new files.
